properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 5:49AM EDT until October 11 at 11:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Avery County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Buncombe County in western North Carolina...
McDowell County in western North Carolina...
Mitchell County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Yancey County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A
few flood- prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 541 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated that the last axis of
heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Isaias is training
over the central Escarpment and northern North Carolina
mountains.  This heavy rainfall will be capable of producing
0.75-1.25 inches of additional rain over the next 60-90 minutes.
This rainfall may exacerbate ongoing high flow and nuisance
flooding conditions and is likely to cause new areas of nuisance
flooding to develop.  Areas of greatest concern include Flat
Creek near Black Mountain and Montreat, the Cane River near
Burnsville, Cane Creek near Bakersville, the headwaters of the
upper Catawba River from Old Fort to Pleasant Gardens to Lake
James, and Grassy Creek and the North Toe River near Spruce Pine.

- If rainfall persists or rates intensify over the next 15-30
minutes, portions of this Flood Advisory may be upgraded to a
Flash Flood Warning. Caution is advised near any stream or other
vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain
develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash flooding
develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation
orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Marion, Spruce Pine, Burnsville, Newland, Black Mountain,
Swannanoa, Fairview In Buncombe County, Old Fort, Banner Elk and
Elk Park.

- Https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:49AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Ashe County in northwestern North Carolina...
Watauga County in northwestern North Carolina...
Southwestern Wilkes County in northwestern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 547 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
light to moderate rainfall. However, flooding is ongoing in the
warned area due to between 4 and locally 7 inches of rain that
fell since Saturday morning.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Fall Creek, Norris Fork, Flat Branch, Elk Creek, Mill Creek,
Dugger Creek, Little Dugger Creek, Laurel Fork, Dutch Creek, Meat
Camp Creek, Brushy Fork, Grassy Creek and Left Prong Stony Fork.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Boone, Blowing Rock, Deep Gap, Todd, Foscoe, Seven Devils and
Aho.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Cleveland, NC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:46AM EDT until October 12 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

(English) Broad River At above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling Springs
affecting Cleveland County.

.Heavy tropical showers will taper off across the Broad River basin
this morning. But runoff from widespread 4 to 6 inches of storm total
rainfall will cause flooding along the Broad River.  Interests all
along the Broad River, even as far upstream as Bat Cave are urged to
monitor river levels and take appropriate action as needed.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River at above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling
Springs.

* WHEN...From this morning to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor Flood Stage. Broad River floodwaters
may be approaching the base of residential home foundations between
Abe's Mountain Rd. and the river. At 14.0 feet, Moderate Flood
Stage. Broad River floodwaters may be inundating the foundations of
homes located between Abe's Mountain Rd. and the river and
threatening residential first floors.  Low-lying roads near the
vicinity of Abe's Mountain may be inundated by floodwaters.  The
Broad River Greenway is experiencing flooding of low-elevation
trails and picnic areas along the river.  Floodwaters may be
impacting local campgrounds near the river as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 11.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 13.5 feet this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.4
feet on 01/25/2010.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued this evening before 600 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Surry, NC; Carroll, VA; Floyd, VA; Patrick, VA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 5:31AM EDT until October 11 at 7:15AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Surry County in northwestern North Carolina...
Southeastern Carroll County in southwestern Virginia...
South Central Floyd County in southwestern Virginia...
Southwestern Patrick County in southwestern Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 715 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Dangerous
flows over low-water crossings. Water has been observed flowing
over a few roadways throughout the night.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 527 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated light to moderate rain
falling across the Advisory area, with minor flooding of small
creeks and streams, as well as low water crossings continuing.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen since Saturday
evening.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Archies Creek and Ararat River. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.5 to 1 inch are expected over the area. This additional rain
will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mount Airy, Fairview, Flat Rock, Hillsville, Dobson and Cana.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Be
especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Southeast; Eastern Interior; Central Interior; Ponce and Vicinity
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 11 at 5:31AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 531 AM AST, Doppler radar was tracking strong showers over
south-central to southeastern Puerto Rico and over the nearshore
waters, moving west-northwest at 20 mph. Thunderstorm formation
possible with these showers.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph. Thunderstorms possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Ponce, Guayama, Coamo, Santa Isabel, Aibonito, Salinas, Cayey,
Villalba, Juana Diaz, Cidra, Arroyo, Patillas, Vazquez, Coco, Los
Llanos, Las Ollas, Jauca and Coqui.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Henderson, NC; Transylvania, NC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:24AM EDT until October 11 at 11:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Transylvania County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 517 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain has recently
departed Transylvania and most of Henderson County. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area. Between
3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen, but only light additional
rain is expected. Most of the flooding is due to run off from
previous rainfall. Mud Creek in Hendersonville is in Minor Flood,
and still rising.

Common, deeper flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to Mud Creek
is developing with lesser impacts to vulnerable property.  More
significant floodwaters are beginning to impact low-lying areas,
including areas of William H. King Memorial Park and the Oklawaha
Greenway, with inundation approximately 2-4 ft deep.  Secondary
roads and outbuildings may be experiencing flooding up to 1-2 ft
deep.
- Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over
the next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all
evacuation orders from local Emergency Management officials.
Only a few inches of water can strand your vehicle and only 6
inches of water can sweep your vehicle away.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hendersonville, Brevard, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat Rock,
Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park, Rosman and Dupont State
Forest.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.
